title: The ubuntu required context is wall-clock brittle: the suite swings 226s to 650s against a 6m per-attempt timeout with one retry
description:
Filed on opum-agent's ruling of 2026-09-30 (after it ruled that a green re-run of the same required job on the same head SHA satisfies the required context, and that this brittleness is a real defect in this repository's own CI, to be taken after the pair).

THE MEASUREMENT. The `lint · typecheck · test (ubuntu-latest)` required context runs `timeout --kill-after=10s 6m bun test --isolate --max-concurrency=1 --timeout=10000`, with ONE retry on a kill or on the known `EEXIST ... epoll_ctl` line. This suite's runtime across the last eight runs of 2026-09-30 swings from **226s to 650s**:

  02:24 failure 250s · 02:30 success 288s · 02:35 success 226s · 02:46 SUCCESS 650s · 06:07 success 263s · 11:36 success 288s · 13:38 success 288s

A run has PASSED at 650s -- two attempts, the second finishing inside its 6m -- so the retry is load-bearing, not decorative. A run fails when BOTH attempts hit the wall.

WHAT IT COSTS. On 2026-09-30 it blocked the DEC-80 release train for an afternoon, on PR opum-ai/lore-cli#446 head `d9a144f7`, three attempts deep:
- attempt 1 (13:53, 11m25s): four tests at exactly their 10s per-test timeout;
- attempt 2 (14:06, 12m37s): the suite wedged after `cli.test.ts` and never finished;
- attempt 3 (14:20, 5m21s): the suite COMPLETED in 286.59s -- the same runtime as the green run, 288s -- with 4887 pass and THREE fail, each failing test at ~10000ms: `A4 registry read-back > the checker unable to read its input`, `release.yml's publish step stages seven of eight tarballs (LCLI-621) > positive control: six platforms at X, then the X-rc.N launcher last`, and `shell-guard as a PreToolUse hook > exits 2 with the rule on stderr for a refused Bash command`.

THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT MATTERS, and the reason this is not "just a flake": the failing tests DIFFER on every attempt, and every one of them is a subprocess-spawning suite -- the family this repository's own notes already describe as flaking at the 10s timeout. Attempt 3 is the sharpest evidence: the suite ran at full speed (286.59s against a 288s green baseline) while three individual tests hung to their wall, which rules out "the runner was slow" as the whole story and points at something the spawning tests contend on. Also ruled out at the time: sibling repositories were green in the same window (opum-doc's CI succeeded at 13:31), and none of the failing tests can be reached from the diff under review.

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN, and must be measured before designing a fix: whether the swing is runner-to-runner variance, a specific contention between spawning tests under `--isolate`, or something about the pinned quest source build the test env sets (`QUEST_SOURCE_REF` is present in the environment of the test step). The duration table above is a same-day snapshot, not a trend -- it should be refreshed when this is worked, because a stale duration table is exactly the trap this task is about.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The cause of the 226s-to-650s runtime swing and of the individual 10s per-test timeouts is identified from fresh evidence -- a refreshed duration table and, for at least one hanging test, the thing it was waiting on -- rather than inferred from this task's snapshot.

The ubuntu required context no longer fails for wall-clock reasons at the observed worst-case duration, proven by a run at or beyond that duration that reports its step conclusions rather than a timeout.

implementationNotes: HYPOTHESIS from the fourth failed attempt, recorded as a hypothesis and not as a finding. Attempt 4 (14:26, 12m27s) failed with a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT set again: `lore agent context --contract opum-agent-workflow/v1` binding-seam tests, an AC1 Constitution-pack test, `cli — init dispatch` and `cli — validate dispatch`, all at ~10000ms. Across four attempts the failing set has changed every time, and the one property they share is now unmistakable: EVERY failing test is one that SPAWNS the lore CLI or another subprocess. A plausible mechanism, untested: bun transpiles TypeScript on first invocation of a file, so the first CLI spawn inside each isolated test file pays that cost; on a runner with a slow disk that exceeds the 10s per-test budget, and WHICH test is first varies with scheduling -- which would explain both the 10s wall and the different names each run. If that is right, the fix is a cache-and-prewarm question (the bun transpile cache or a warm-up invocation before the suite) rather than a timeout question, and the workflow comment forbidding a timeout raise would stay intact. NOT MEASURED -- the first thing this task should do is test it, e.g. by timing a single CLI spawn cold versus warm on the runner.

MECHANISM CANDIDATE, and it is repository-specific. Read .github/actions/setup-quest/action.yml: when the declared quest version is not on npm -- the state RIGHT NOW, since quest 0.12.0 is unpublished -- the fallback builds quest-cli at the pinned ref and puts a SHIM on PATH whose entire body is: exec bun run "$dest/src/cli/main.ts" "$@". So EVERY quest invocation is a full bun transpile-and-start of a TypeScript CLI tree, per call, with no compiled artifact and no warm entry point. That is the shape of the failures rather than a guess about them: every test that has failed across five attempts is one that SPWNS a CLI (quest or lore), the failures are always at the 10s per-test wall rather than at an assertion, and which tests fail varies with scheduling. FACT: the shim is what I read, verbatim. INFERENCE, not measured: that a cold quest invocation sometimes exceeds 10s on these runners. A single measurement settles it -- time `quest --version` cold on the runner, and time a corpus of spawning tests with a pre-built quest. If it holds, the fix is in setup-quest (build once, e.g. a compiled artifact or a pre-warmed entry point) and NOT in the timeout, which keeps the workflow comment intact. NOTE the contrast that makes this repository the only sufferer: sibling repos install quest from npm or do not drive it per-test, and their CI was green throughout this window (opum-agent 14:35, opum-doc 13:31).

SHIM HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, and the real mechanism found in this repository's own workflow comment. Both recorded here so neither is re-derived.

MEASURED, locally, reproducing setup-quest's fallback exactly (blob-filtered no-checkout clone of quest-cli, sparse checkout of src/package.json/bun.lock/tsconfig.json, checkout at ec79b543, bun install --frozen-lockfile, then the verbatim shim `exec bun run "$dest/src/cli/main.ts" "$@"`):
- `quest --version` through the shim: **0.03s**, and identical cold and warm -- there is no per-invocation transpile penalty to remove, so a "build once" change to setup-quest would buy nothing.
- The two tests that hit their 10s timeout on CI, run locally: **146ms** and **585ms**.
- The three failing files under the CI's exact flags (`--isolate --max-concurrency=1 --timeout=10000`): **90 pass, 0 fail, 9.46s**.

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM, and it is already written down in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s test step: a Bun/Linux **epoll registration race** when isolated test files concurrently construct streams over the process stdio fds (LCLI-507). The comment records TWO presentations: it can print `error: EEXIST: file already exists, epoll_ctl` and exit non-zero quickly, OR it can hang before ever printing that line, in which case `timeout --kill-after=10s 6m` kills it six minutes later with exit 124. The retry guard fires on those two signals only. The same comment notes that LCLI-648 moved the pin from 1.3.14 to 1.4.2 WITHOUT re-measuring the race, so the retry was kept on faith -- which is the likely reason it is biting now rather than occasionally.

THE GAP, measured on 2026-09-30's five failing attempts on PR #446: there is a THIRD presentation the guard does not cover. The race hangs a handful of tests, each is killed at its own per-test 10s budget, the suite COMPLETES with those as failures, and the exit code is therefore NEITHER 124 NOR accompanied by the EEXIST line -- so the retry never fires and the job fails on its first and only run. attempts 3 and 4's logs consist SOLELY of `(fail) <name> [10000.xxms]` lines -- every failure's recorded duration is at the per-test timeout -- and there is not one assertion-duration failure in them.

PROPOSED FIX, and it stays inside the existing design: extend the retry condition to fire when the log shows a failing test whose duration is at or above the per-test timeout. A genuine product-test assertion failure carries a short duration, so "Product-test failures remain fatal without a retry" is preserved exactly; no timeout is raised, `--isolate` and `--max-concurrency=1` stay, and the fix does not model a longer wait as the answer. It must be proven both ways as this repository requires: a deliberate artificial hang retries, and a deliberate assertion failure does not.
